lines.en: Hello, Zoe. Sit down, please. What is the problem, and how long has it been going on?
lines.pt: Olá, Zoe. Sente-se, por favor. Qual é o problema, e há quanto tempo isso acontece?

lines.en: I’ve had a fever since Monday, and I’ve been coughing for five days. It began with a cold.
lines.pt: Estou com febre desde segunda, e estou tossindo há cinco dias. Começou com um resfriado.

lines.en: I see. Have you been taking anything for it? Any painkillers, or perhaps some medicine from the pharmacy?
lines.pt: Entendo. Você tem tomado alguma coisa? Algum analgésico, ou talvez remédio da farmácia?

lines.en: Only aspirin, twice a day. It brings the temperature down, but the fever comes back after a few hours.
lines.pt: Só aspirin, duas vezes por dia. Ele baixa a temperatura, mas a febre volta depois de algumas horas.

lines.en: Do you have any other symptoms? A sore throat, a headache, or have you felt dizzy at all?
lines.pt: Você tem outros sintomas? Dor de garganta, dor de cabeça, ou já se sentiu tonta?

lines.en: My throat has been sore for a week, and I’ve felt really tired. I have not been able to work properly.
lines.pt: Minha garganta está inflamada há uma semana, e tenho me sentido muito cansada. Não consigo trabalhar direito.

lines.en: Let me listen to your chest. Breathe in deeply. It sounds a little tight, but I do not think it is serious.
lines.pt: Deixe-me ouvir seu peito. Respire fundo. Parece um pouco apertado, mas acho que não é grave.

lines.en: That is a relief. How long will it take to get over it? I have an important trip next week.
lines.pt: Que alívio. Quanto tempo vai levar para eu me recuperar? Tenho uma viagem importante na semana que vem.

lines.en: Most people recover within ten days. I will write a prescription, and you must rest and drink plenty of water.
lines.pt: A maioria das pessoas se recupera em dez dias. Vou fazer uma receita, e você precisa descansar e beber bastante água.

lines.en: Should I stay at home until the fever has gone? And when should I come back if I am not better?
lines.pt: Devo ficar em casa até a febre passar? E quando devo voltar se eu não melhorar?

lines.en: Stay home until it has gone for a full day. If the symptoms persist after a week, please call us again.
lines.pt: Fique em casa até a febre ter passado por um dia inteiro. Se os sintomas persistirem depois de uma semana, ligue de novo.

facts.label: Saúde: sintomas e duração
facts.sub: Use o present perfect com since e for: I’ve had a fever since Monday. I’ve been coughing for five days.

facts.label: Desde quando
facts.sub: Since + ponto no tempo: since Monday, since last week. I’ve had a fever since Monday. Use o present perfect, não o presente.

facts.label: Por quanto tempo
facts.sub: For + período: for five days, for a week. I’ve been coughing for five days. Use a forma contínua para ações que continuam.

items.s: We say “I’ve had a fever since Monday.”
We say “I am here since Monday.”
items.why: Use the present perfect: I have been here since Monday.

items.s: For is used with a period, such as five days.

answers: We say “I’ve had a fever since Monday.” → Verdadeiro (Since gives the starting point.)
We say “I am here since Monday.” → Falso (Use the present perfect: I have been here since Monday.)
For is used with a period, such as five days. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: At the clinic · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey Thursday morning in London. The waiting room of a small clinic is full. People cough and check their phones. Zoe has been feeling terrible for days. Finally, a nurse calls her name. Dr. Elena is waiting in her office.

“Hello, Zoe. Sit down, please. What is the problem, and how long has it been going on?” says Elena. “I’ve had a fever since Monday, and I’ve been coughing for five days. It began with a cold.” says Zoe. “I see. Have you been taking anything for it? Any painkillers, or perhaps some medicine from the pharmacy?” says Elena.
